Jennie fills an aquarium, in the shape of a rectangular prism that is $50\,\text{cm}$ long and $25\,\text{cm}$ wide, with water from a tap. What is the rate of change of the water level if the volume is increasing at a rate of $250\,{\text{cm}}^{3}/\text{h}?$

The water level is increasing at a rate of
{{field-1}}
$\text{cm}/\text{h}.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $x,y,z$ be the dimensions of the rectangular prism, let $V$ be its volume. We are given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =50\,\text{cm}, \\ y & =25\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, we know that

$$
\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=250\,{\text{cm}}^{3}/\text{h}.
$$

We would like to find $\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}$ when $x=50\,\text{cm}$ and $y=25\,\text{cm}.$

We start with the formula for the volume of the rectangular prism:

$$
V=xyz
$$

Substituting the known values, we get

$$
V=(50)(25)z=1250z.
$$

Now, we differentiate with respect to time using the chain rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1250z) \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =1250(\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}).\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plug in the known value into the above expression. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}250 & =1250(\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}) \\ \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} & =0.2\,\text{cm}\text{/h}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the water level is increasing at a rate of $0.2\,\text{cm}/\text{h}.$
